poster_title: LeanRAG: Knowledge-Graph-Based Generation with Semantic Aggregation and Hierarchical Retrieval
authors: Yaoze Zhang, Rong Wu, Pinlong Cai, Xiaoman Wang, Guohang Yan, Song Mao, Ding Wang, Botian Shi
paper_info: 2023, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, Zhejiang University, East China Normal University

panels.headline: Contextually flawed or incomplete information in RAG
content: RAG enhances LLMs by leveraging external knowledge, but often suffers from contextually flawed or incomplete information.
Knowledge graph-based RAG methods improve local context preservation over disconnected text chunks.
High-level summary nodes in hierarchical knowledge graphs exist as 'semantic islands' without explicit relational connections.
The retrieval process in existing methods remains structurally unaware, often degenerating into an inefficient flat search over nodes.
LeanRAG aims to address these limitations by integrating semantic aggregation and structure-guided retrieval.

panels.headline: Semantic Aggregation Algorithm
content: Introduces a semantic aggregation algorithm that forms entity clusters and constructs explicit relations among summaries, creating a fully navigable semantic network.

Employs a bottom-up, structure-guided retrieval strategy that anchors queries to fine-grained entities and traverses the graph's semantic pathways to gather concise, contextually comprehensive evidence sets.

panels.headline: Four Challenging QA Benchmarks
content: Conducted extensive experiments on four challenging QA benchmarks with different domains.
Evaluated the performance of LeanRAG in terms of response quality and retrieval efficiency.
Used datasets from various domains to ensure the robustness of the method.
Compared LeanRAG with several state-of-the-art baseline methods.
The experiments were designed to test both the quality and efficiency of the responses.

panels.headline: Significantly Outperformed Baselines
content: LeanRAG significantly outperformed existing methods in response quality.
Reduced retrieval redundancy by 46% compared to existing methods.
panels.figure_caption: Evaluation scores (1-10 scale) of LeanRAG compared to baseline methods, assessed by a LLM.

panels.headline: State-of-the-Art Performance
content: LeanRAG effectively addresses the limitations of existing knowledge graph-based RAG methods by integrating semantic aggregation and structure-guided retrieval.
The framework significantly improves the quality and efficiency of LLM responses in QA tasks.
LeanRAG achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple QA tasks, demonstrating both high response quality and retrieval efficiency.
The effectiveness of the method may be limited by the quality and completeness of the input knowledge graph.
Future work will focus on enhancing the robustness and scalability of the framework.
